review_notes: Read the whole target file and the upstream definitions in RealPolynomialChartSubstitution.lean (dualEvalLie, dualEvalLie_base/tangent, polynomialFirstJetHom, polynomialFirstJet_base, polynomialLogDerivative), plus a grep of other uses. I did not run Lean. The `change` steps rely on defeq of `.coord` of `polynomialFirstJetHom` (a `NilpotentLieBCHGroup.map`) with `dualEvalLie ... coord`; that is assumed from the code compiling, and I did not inspect `NilpotentLieBCHGroup.map`. The proposed lemmas would likely need a `rfl`/`change`-based proof, and I have not checked it compiles. I did not make claims about loops. Only two findings, both about the simp interface.

findings.excerpt:
change dualBaseLinear (dualEvalLie t h A.coord) ∈ U
    rw [dualEvalLie_base]
findings.problem: Four near-identical blocks (and two more in polynomialLogDerivative_mem_of_coefficients, lines 38-44) each use `change` to expose `dualEvalLie`, then `rw` with the non-simp lemmas `dualEvalLie_base` and `dualEvalLie_tangent`. The simp interface has `polynomialFirstJet_base` for `dualBaseHom (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P)`. It has nothing for the coordinate-level terms `dualBaseLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P).coord` and `dualTangentLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P).coord`, which are what the dual lemmas' hypotheses actually mention. So simp cannot normalise these terms. Callers must unfold by `change` through `NilpotentLieBCHGroup.map`, which is fragile and repeated. `dualEvalLie_base` and `dualEvalLie_tangent` are also left without `@[simp]`, although the neighbouring `dualEvalLie_tmul` and `directionalDerivative_tmul` are simp.
findings.proposed_change: In RealPolynomialChartSubstitution.lean, next to `polynomialFirstJet_base`, add simp lemmas for the packaged form. One is `dualBaseLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P).coord = eval t P.coord`, proved by `dualEvalLie_base t h P.coord`. The other is `dualTangentLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P).coord = eval t (directionalDerivative h P.coord)`, proved by `dualEvalLie_tangent t h P.coord`. Both are oriented towards the simpler `eval` form, so nothing loops. Consider also tagging `dualEvalLie_base` and `dualEvalLie_tangent` `@[simp]`. Then each `have haU/hcU/haV/hcV` collapses to `by simpa using (eval_mem_iff_coefficients U.toSubmodule _).mpr hAU t`, or a direct `exact` with the rewritten statement. The two bullets of `polynomialLogDerivative_mem_of_coefficients` shrink the same way.
findings.benefit: Removes six copies of the `change … rw …` boilerplate and the reliance on definitional unfolding of `.coord`. Future uses of the first-jet homomorphism get the base and tangent components in canonical `eval` form from `simp`.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem dualEvalLie_base (t h : σ → ℚ) (p : VectorPolynomial σ ℚ L) :
    dualBaseLinear (dualEvalLie t h p) = eval t p

@[simp] theorem polynomialFirstJet_base (t h : σ → ℚ) (P : PolynomialGroup σ hnil) :
    dualBaseHom (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P) = polynomialValueHom t P
dualTangentLinear (dualEvalLie t h p) = eval t (directionalDerivative h p)

findings.problem: `polynomialLogDerivative` is a plain `def` with no unfolding or simp lemma. Every transfer from the dual-group statements to the polynomial statements therefore needs `simpa only [..., polynomialFirstJet_base, polynomialLogDerivative]`, with the definition name passed to simp to unfold it. This happens here at lines 58, 61 and 105, and also in `polynomialFirstJet_insertion` in RealPolynomialChartSubstitution.lean (line 193). The user must remember which simp set bridges `dualLogDerivative (polynomialFirstJetHom …)` and `polynomialLogDerivative`. The unfolding direction also exposes `dualLogDerivative` for any caller using plain `simp`. The canonical form is the opposite direction, folding into `polynomialLogDerivative`.
findings.proposed_change: Add one equation lemma, e.g. `polynomialLogDerivative_eq : polynomialLogDerivative t h P = dualLogDerivative (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P) := rfl`. Use it as a named bridge in these `simpa only` calls instead of the bare definition. Optionally add a `@[simp]` lemma that folds `dualLogDerivative (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P)` back to `polynomialLogDerivative t h P`. Together with `polynomialFirstJet_base` this gives a single normal form. Make sure the fold direction and the unfold lemma are not both simp.
findings.benefit: The bridge between the dual and polynomial layers becomes a documented rewrite rule, not an unfold of a definition repeated in four proofs. Plain `simp` would then normalise to the polynomial-level notation that the theorem statements use.

evidence.excerpt:
noncomputable def polynomialLogDerivative (t h : σ → ℚ) (P : PolynomialGroup σ hnil) : L :=
  dualLogDerivative (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P)
